issues.description: Directs() still dereferences i.publicEnd on a nil receiver inside the closure
issues.detail: In ir_imports.go Directs(), the nil guard sets `slice` to nil before reading `i.files`, but the returned closure still captures `i` and reads `i.publicEnd`/`i.weakEnd` etc. when invoked. For a nil receiver `slice` is empty so the closure won't fire, but if `i` is non-nil and `i.files` is non-empty while other fields are inconsistent, the original semantics are preserved — yet the new code path silently returns an empty Indexer instead of panicking when callers expect data. Reviewer should confirm tests cover the closure invocation, not only Len().

issues.description: FeatureSet() on nil *File returns FeatureSet{} but other methods like Deprecated still panic on nil
issues.detail: ir_file.go adds nil checks to many accessors (Imports, Types, Options, FeatureSet, Symbols, etc.) but leaves File.Deprecated(), InternedPath(), Path(), Package(), InternedPackage(), ImportFor(), and File.AST() unguarded. The zero test only covers a subset, so callers of those methods on a nil *File will still panic. This is an inconsistent contract — either guard all accessors or document which are nil-safe.

issues.description: Test reflection loop skips methods returning functions, weakening coverage
issues.detail: In zero_test.go testZeroAny, the loop `continue`s when a return value's Kind is Func, so any accessor that returns a closure/iter.Seq (e.g., AllMembers returning iter.Seq[Member]) is never actually exercised. The whole point — verifying the closure doesn't panic when invoked on zero — is bypassed. Consider invoking iter.Seq returns with a no-op yield to ensure the inner body doesn't panic.

issues.description: AllMembers index counter `i` is captured but reset semantics unclear on repeated iteration
issues.detail: ir_file.go AllMembers declares `i := 0` outside the returned iter.Seq closure. If the returned Seq is iterated multiple times, `i` continues from where it left off, producing wrong IDs on the second pass. This bug predates the diff but the refactor touches the function; worth fixing while in the area by moving `i := 0` inside the iterx.Map closure scope or resetting per iteration.

issues.description: Repeated `var x; if !IsZero { x = ... }` pattern is verbose; consider a helper
issues.detail: ir_type.go and ir_file.go duplicate the same five-line guard pattern roughly a dozen times. A small helper like `func safeSlice[T any](z zeroable, get func() []T) []T` or restructuring around an early-return zero Indexer would reduce repetition and make future accessors harder to forget to guard. Not blocking, but a maintenance smell as more methods are added.

issues.description: ValueNodeIndex sentinel change from 0 to -1 may break existing callers
issues.detail: Element.ValueNodeIndex previously returned whatever the search produced (potentially 0) for any element. The new code returns -1 for the zero element. Callers like the doc-comment example `e.Value().MessageKeys().At(e.ValueNodeIndex())` would now pass -1 into At(), which likely panics. Verify no existing call site treats the return as an unconditional valid index.

review.summary: The PR adds defensive nil/zero guards across many ir accessors and a reflection-based zero test. The approach is sound and the test scaffolding is nice, but the nil-safety contract is inconsistent — several File accessors (Deprecated, Path, AST, ImportFor) remain unguarded, and the test's reflection loop skips closure-returning methods, so iter.Seq accessors like AllMembers aren't truly verified. The repeated `var x; if !IsZero` guard pattern would benefit from a helper. Also worth confirming the new -1 sentinel from ValueNodeIndex doesn't break any callers feeding it back into At().
